model: Attributable underlying-profit AFFO-style FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual note (staff costs) employee share-based payments HK$54m consolidated (Hang Lung Properties option scheme; 0010.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:8982), x64% attributable = HK$35m. No equity-award taxes (HK net-share settlement not used). SBC is already expensed inside underlying net profit; the engine margin is grossed up by the same 0.5pp so the charge is made exactly once.
inputs.attributable_share_basis: Shareholders' equity / total equity at 30-Jun-2026 = 102,299 / 159,330 = 64.2% (FY2025: 98,881 / 155,267 = 63.7%). HLG owns 65.1% of Hang Lung Properties (FY2025 AR subsidiaries list, line 10769) plus some directly held HK property; the attributable share of consolidated economics is therefore taken as 64%.
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,361.62m shares on issue, unchanged since at least FY2017; no buybacks, no dilutive HLG-level securities (HLP's options are at the subsidiary and their cost is in the SBC line). Held flat.
inputs.stream_definition: Revenue base = 64% x FY2025 consolidated property-leasing + hotel revenue (9,853 + 297 = 10,150) = 6,496. 'EBITDA margin' is NOT EBITDA: it is attributable underlying net profit from leasing + hotels AFTER tax, AFTER all interest (including interest the accounts capitalise into development), AFTER minorities, BEFORE SBC, over that revenue. FY2025: leasing+hotels underlying attributable 2,456 (2,529 - 73), less attributable capitalised interest net of tax ~471 (backed out of the company's own 'payout ratio after deducting interest capitalized' of 59% on HK$1,171m dividends) = 1,985; plus 35 SBC = 2,020 / 6,496 = 31.1%. cash_tax_rate is 0 because the stream is already post-tax; D&A is 0 because IAS 40 investment property is not depreciated (hotel/PPE depreciation of HK$150m consolidated is already inside underlying profit). Capex line = attributable maintenance/AEI capex (est. 3.85% of attributable revenue, ~HK$250m) plus the equity-funded share (~70%) of committed development capex; the remaining ~30% is assumed debt-funded, whose interest cost then appears in the margin path. last_fcf 1,735 = 1,985 - 250 maintenance: the recurring attributable AFFO before growth capex (HK$1.27/share vs HK$0.86 DPS).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in HKD (the flows are post-interest, so discount at CoE, never WACC, and hold net debt at zero): HKD risk-free ~4.0% (HKD peg tracks USD 10-year), equity beta ~1.0 for a 30%-geared property holdco, ERP 5.5%, plus 1.0pp for ~69% of net assets sitting in RMB / mainland China regulatory risk = 10.5%. Same CoE in every scenario so risk is charged once (through the scenario paths and weights).
inputs.lease_treatment: Lease liabilities are immaterial (HK$284m at 30-Jun-2026) and their interest is inside underlying profit. The Westlake 66 Expansion 20-year lease (~RMB3.2bn fixed payments from April 2028) is an expansion with its own rent; treated as value-neutral and not modelled separately.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, by valuing only the attributable stream: every line is HLG's own 'attributable to shareholders' figure or 64% of a consolidated figure. No NCI deduction in the bridge. FY0 stream ties to reported underlying net profit attributable to shareholders (2,407) less property-sales losses (+49 add-back, valued separately via inventory) less attributable capitalised interest (471).
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: routed per dcf-methods SKILL.md as a REIT-like property investor (IAS 40 fair value, internally managed) inside a holdco. A consolidated owner-FCF DCF is wrong here on three counts: (1) consolidated FCF belongs 36% to Hang Lung Properties' minorities; (2) interest (~HK$1.9bn/yr paid, HK$984m of it capitalised in FY2025) sits in financing, so reported FCF is unlevered while the debt is a holdco-and-subsidiary mix; (3) reported net income is dominated by revaluations. So the flow valued is the post-interest, post-tax, post-minority underlying profit with capitalised interest treated as a real expense (an AFFO analogue), less maintenance and equity-funded development capex, capitalised at a 10.5% HKD cost of equity with net debt held at zero. NAV/NTA was considered and rejected as the headline: book NAV is HK$75.1/share (30-Jun-2026) against a price of roughly 0.16x book at valuation date, and that discount has persisted for a decade because the assets earn an underlying ROE of ~2.4%; a NAV model would print +500% and be meaningless, exactly the NZL.NZ trap. NAV is kept as a memo only. Property sales (HK luxury and mainland residential) are excluded from the recurring stream and valued once, in the equity bridge, as attributable properties-for-sale inventory at a realisation haircut. No buybacks (buyback_cash 0) and none authorised; the flat count is the natural state. First valuation of this ticker; no prior DCF.

equity_bridge.item: Attributable properties for sale, realisable value
equity_bridge.note: Properties for sale HK$13,854m consolidated at 30-Jun-2026 (interim balance sheet, 0010.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:1776) x 64% attributable = 8,867; x 0.85 realisation (selling costs, LAT/tax, recent sub-cost mainland sales and a HK$124m H1-26 provision) = 7,537; discounted ~3 years at 10.5% (x0.74) = 5,580. Conservative in one respect: the debt that funds this inventory keeps its interest inside the perpetual stream, so the interest saving from repaying it with sale proceeds (~HK$1.5bn PV) is NOT credited.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (1.4%) diverges sharply from reported EPS (-20% 3yr; FY2020 negative so 5yr undefined) and underlying EPS (-7% 3yr: 2.20 FY2022 -> 1.77 FY2025). Reported EPS is revaluation noise; underlying EPS fell because interest costs rose and development properties stopped capitalising interest. The FCF CAGRs (28%/42%) are unlevered, consolidated and start from land-acquisition troughs (FY2020 FCF 636), so they are not a growth signal. SBC is ~0.5% of revenue and interest income is negligible (HK$41m), so owner FCF ~= reported FCF; the history does not move on the SBC adjustment.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue figures are consolidated total (leasing + hotels + property sales). Leasing revenue is the cleaner series: 9,853 FY2025 vs 10,033 FY2024 (-2%); H1 FY2026 5,151 vs 4,912 (+5%, of which ~4pp RMB appreciation).

base.margin_note: FY0 31.1% (post-interest, post-tax, pre-SBC). Dips to 30.5% in FY2026 as Westlake 66 (opened 28-Apr-2026) starts expensing its interest and opex before its rent matures; recovers to 34% by year 7 as Westlake 66, the Plaza 66 Pavilion Extension and Xi Zhe Wuxi hotel lease up on an already-paid-for asset base. Average cost of debt 3.7% held.
base.capex_note: FY2026-27 carry the tail of HK$4.4bn consolidated capital commitments (+HK$0.9bn JV injections) at 30-Jun-2026; development then reverts to maintenance/AEI (3.85%) plus ~1.65pp of modest equity-funded growth/asset-enhancement.

scenario_narratives.base: Mainland luxury retail keeps its gradual, selective recovery (H1-26 mall rent +6% RMB, tenant sales +17%, occupancy 96%) while mainland offices (81% occupied, revenue -11%) stabilise rather than recover. Westlake 66 ramps over 2026-28 and is the main source of the ~6%/yr leasing growth in FY2026-27; HK retail and office are flat-to-slightly-up. Development spend falls to maintenance plus modest AEI once the HK$4.4bn commitment tail is paid, so attributable FCFE rises from ~HK$0.9bn in FY2026 to ~HK$2.3bn by the end of the decade. Dividend held at HK$0.86. Property inventory is sold down over ~3 years near book.
scenario_narratives.bull: A stronger mainland consumption cycle and RMB appreciation (69% of net assets are RMB) lift mall rents faster, Westlake 66 and Wuxi lease up ahead of plan, mainland office vacancy turns, and HK retail benefits from rising visitor arrivals. Rates fall, cutting the 3.7% average cost of debt. Margin reaches 36.5% and growth runs 3-8%; HLP's stated shift to asset-light management lets capex stay at maintenance levels.
scenario_narratives.bear: Mainland luxury spending relapses (consumer deleveraging, policy shift, or tariff/geopolitical shock from the Middle East conflict flagged in the H1-26 outlook), mainland office oversupply keeps rents falling, HK office reversions stay negative, and the RMB weakens against the HKD peg. Westlake 66 leases slowly while its interest is already expensed, so margins drift to 28.5%. Management keeps committing capital to new mainland projects at low returns (the pattern that took underlying ROE to ~2.4%), holding capex at 6% of revenue. Inventory realises well below book.
scenario_narratives.base_weight_reason: Recurring rental franchise with 96% mall occupancy and no balance-sheet stress (net debt/equity 30.5%, 3.0-year tenor, HK$18.5bn undrawn) — the central outcome is slow, steady growth.
scenario_narratives.bull_weight_reason: Needs several things together: mainland luxury recovery, office stabilisation, RMB strength and capex discipline.
scenario_narratives.bear_weight_reason: China consumption/property exposure, a decade of falling underlying EPS, and a controlling family with a record of reinvesting at low returns rather than returning capital.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% for concentrated mainland-China retail/office exposure, falling underlying EPS since FY2022 and controlled-holdco capital allocation; bull cut to 25% because it needs mainland consumption, office absorption, RMB and capex discipline to all go right; base 50% reflects a stable, highly occupied rental franchise with an unstressed balance sheet.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value what HLG's shareholders actually own: their 64% share of the group's recurring rental profit after interest (including capitalised interest), tax and minorities, less the capital needed to maintain and grow it, discounted at an HKD cost of equity with no further debt deduction, plus attributable residential inventory at a realisation haircut. Book NAV (HK$75.1/share) is a memo only: it has never been a price anchor for this name because the assets earn ~2.4% on book.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mainland China luxury retail demand (most of leasing operating profit) and mainland office oversupply
RMB/HKD translation: ~69% of net assets and ~68% of revenue are RMB
Interest rates: HK$55.6bn gross debt at 3.7% average cost; each 100bp ~HK$0.36bn attributable pre-tax
Capital allocation: continued low-return development spend by the controlling family instead of distributions
Holdco discount on the HLP stake may persist regardless of underlying value
valuation_philosophy.holdco_lookthrough_memo: Cross-check 2026-10-09: HLG's 65.1% of Hang Lung Properties (0101.HK, ~4.5bn shares) was worth ~HK$19.4bn at HLP's own market price against an HLG market cap of ~HK$16.7bn, so HLG trades at a >15% discount to its listed HLP stake alone, before its directly held HK property. The market is capitalising the attributable stream at roughly 12-13% with little growth; this model uses a 10.5% CoE and explicit capex. Even the bear case sits above the price, so the gap is a discount-rate / capital-allocation-trust gap, not a cash-flow gap.
